scope.question: Do the Open580 and proprietary580 Linux wrappers provide a GPU/RM-domain selector and two distinct nv_file_private callbacks suitable for a same-process dual-RM broker?
scope.method: Read-only comparison of pinned R580.178.04 wrapper sources, callback ABI, RM initialization sources, Kbuild fragments, and the extracted proprietary RM object symbol table.

proprietary_wrapper_and_core.note: No enclosing proprietary package archive hash was available in the inspected tree; every cited wrapper/config/object file is individually SHA-256 pinned in sources.

flavor_and_build_selection.observation: The literal NV_OPEN_KERNEL_MODULES has no textual occurrence in the pinned Open580 or extracted proprietary580 source/package trees searched (C/H, Kbuild, Makefile, and make fragments). The actual NV_KERNEL_MODULES variable is only a whitespace-separated list of module targets. Open and proprietary nvidia.Kbuild and nvidia-sources.Kbuild are byte-identical. Both nvidia.Kbuild files link nvidia/nv-kernel.o_binary into nvidia.ko; this is a build-time core-object choice, not a per-GPU runtime branch.
flavor_and_build_selection.source_built_object_caveat: The R580 archive also contains src/nvidia/Makefile, which builds source lists from srcs.mk to $(OUTPUTDIR)/nv-kernel.o. Therefore the suffix/name nv-kernel.o_binary alone does not prove proprietary provenance. In this archive the stock kernel-open Kbuild expects a sibling nv-kernel.o_binary path, which is absent from the extracted kernel-open/nvidia directory; the proprietary package supplies a 112,677,456-byte ELF relocatable object at its nvidia/nv-kernel.o_binary path. A custom source build may populate the expected core object, but no such build was performed here.
flavor_and_build_selection.module_license_observation: Open wrapper kernel-open/nvidia/nv.c line 112 declares MODULE_LICENSE("Dual MIT/GPL"); proprietary wrapper nvidia/nv.c line 112 declares MODULE_LICENSE("NVIDIA"). The wrapper source also differs in OS integration/features (for example DMA_BUF namespace imports and confidential-compute handling); these differences do not create a backend selector. MODULE_LICENSE is module metadata/licensing declaration, not RM routing logic.
flavor_and_build_selection.interpretation: Do not use an imagined NV_OPEN_KERNEL_MODULES switch or MODULE_LICENSE value as a runtime flavor selector. Select/link the intended RM core explicitly and ensure the final module's license metadata matches the actually linked core and redistribution terms.

rm_initialization_and_global_state.observation: Open and proprietary nv.c wrappers call the same-signature rm_init_rm(stack) from the nvidia module-init path before nv_module_state_init. The shared nv.h declares rm_init_rm(nvidia_stack_t*) with no GPU/backend argument. Open RM's rm_init_rm calls RmInitRm(); RmInitRm calls coreInitializeRm(); coreInitializeRm creates the system object and calls rmapiInitialize. rmapi.c has one g_resServ plus static g_RmApiList, initialization guard, and lock globals; rmapiInitialize constructs that one global server.
rm_initialization_and_global_state.proprietary_object_symbols: The extracted proprietary 580.178.04 core object exports rm_init_rm, rm_ioctl, and rm_shutdown_rm and imports nv_get_file_private/nv_put_file_private. The open source tree defines matching RM entry points. This is direct symbol-table evidence of one core API contract, not a same-version dual-link test.
rm_initialization_and_global_state.interpretation: Calling rm_init_rm through two wrapper callbacks cannot create two RM namespaces when both calls reach one linked RM image: the normal initialization target is process/module-global RM state. Independent state-isolated RM images require separate global state and symbol/link isolation, or a substantive refactor; callbacks alone are insufficient.

file_private_and_register_fd.observation: The Open580 and proprietary580 nv.h files are byte-identical. They declare nv_get_file_private(fd, ctl, os_private) with no RM-domain parameter. Their nv.c callback bodies are byte-for-byte identical: fget(fd), require this wrapper's NV_MAJOR_DEVICE_NUMBER, check the single control-device minor when ctl=true (or a regular-device minor in its table), then return &nvlfp->nvfp. Each open allocates one nv_linux_file_private_t/nvfp; different open file descriptions can therefore yield different nvfp pointers, but dup shares the same file description. The structure has no explicit RM-domain selector. NV_ESC_REGISTER_FD calls this callback for a control fd and stores a single ctl_nvfp/ctl_nvfp_priv link in the source nvfp; it rejects an existing link, self-link, and a control nvfp that is itself linked, and the association remains until close.
file_private_and_register_fd.proprietary_binary_evidence: The proprietary R580 RM object imports nv_get_file_private and nv_put_file_private. The proprietary RM source for REGISTER_FD is unavailable in the inspected tree; the Open580 source establishes the exact open implementation, while the binary imports establish callback ABI dependence, not its internal control flow.
file_private_and_register_fd.implication: A single wrapper can supply distinct per-open nvfp records, but its stock callback resolves by OS fd/file only. It cannot tell which RM core is calling it, and REGISTER_FD provides one lifetime-held control association rather than a backend/core selector. Multiple callbacks aimed at the same wrapper function do not solve this.

gpu_selection_and_control_fd.observation: For a regular GPU node, nvidia_open resolves its minor through the module's device table and stores that nv_linux_state in this open's file-private. The control path instead calls nvidia_ctl_open, which stores the module-global nv_ctl_device. nvidia_ioctl derives pNv from that file-private and sends default RM ioctls through the single linked rm_ioctl(sp, nv, &nvlfp->nvfp, ...). Open RM's NV_ESC_RM_ALLOC forces root classes to NV01_ROOT_CLIENT and requires the control device.
gpu_selection_and_control_fd.inference: The wrapper can identify the physical device for an ioctl associated with a regular GPU node, but root-client creation arrives on the singleton control node and has no GPU identity to select a second RM. Later hClient/handles are plain RM-domain scoped numbers; the prior namespace artifact establishes they need a separate backend tag outside the stock ABI.

architecture_verdict.direct_answer: An unmodified shared R580 wrapper cannot route one process's requests to two RM cores by GPU and cannot expose two backend-specific file-private domains merely by opening files twice. It can allocate multiple distinct nvfp instances, but stock ioctl dispatch invokes one linked rm_ioctl implementation and stock RM initialization creates one global g_resServ domain.
minimum_independent_adaptation_seams: RM core isolation: independently instantiate or namespace the RM globals/entry points, including g_resServ, g_RmApiList and associated process-global managers/locks. Two callbacks entering the same stock globals remain one namespace.

Wrapper/file routing: carry an explicit backend/domain identity from a backend-specific control endpoint or broker handle into ioctl dispatch and into the OS callback/file-private lifetime. A GPU minor alone cannot select the root client because root allocation is control-device-only. REGISTER_FD must retain distinct per-domain control links and cleanup ownership.
reuse_candidates: The Open580 and proprietary580 wrapper ABI headers and nvidia.Kbuild source lists are byte-identical; the per-open file-private allocator, fd validation, and file lifetime mechanisms are reusable foundations for one deliberately extended wrapper.

The open RM source exposes the callback and dispatch seam in osapi.c/escape.c and provides a source-built core Makefile; it can guide a clean broker interface without reverse engineering proprietary code.
A single RM core remains the normal coherent arrangement for all GPUs attached to it; per-GPU pNv selection does not by itself justify two RM instances.
not_proven: No same-version Open580-source plus proprietary580-object dual-link experiment was run. The proprietary object exports the same rm_* symbols that Open580 source defines, so duplicate-symbol failure is a strong static prediction; the existing recorded link failure is OpenR595 source plus proprietary R580 object and is cross-version evidence only.
No public libcuda/CUDA user-library routing, handle translation, UVM, GPU enumeration merge, physical GPU behavior, or runtime cleanup was tested.
Whether two full RM images can be safely isolated in one kernel module remains unknown; duplicating g_resServ alone would not prove isolation of all core globals and callback lifetimes.

checks.command: rg -n --hidden --no-ignore -F NV_OPEN_KERNEL_MODULES <Open580 tree> <proprietary580 tree> (excluding object/binary/log files)
checks.result: No textual matches in the inspected source/package trees.
Both Kbuild fragments are identical byte-for-byte (SHA-256 adee2cdb... and a4fbda68...).

checks.command: Python source comparison of nv_get_file_private function bodies

checks.result: ELF64 x86-64 relocatable; defined rm_init_rm/rm_ioctl/rm_shutdown_rm and undefined nv_get_file_private/nv_put_file_private.
All listed source paths exist and are pinned individually; no driver build, module load, install, hardware test, or PC3 access.
